sentences.text: This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .20,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by her.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 04.01.2023 at about 04.45 a.m., she was travelling in Tempo Traveller bearing Regn.No.KA-13- B-5706 which was proceeding on nice road from Hosur to Tumkur Road and when they reached near Kodigehalli Bridge, Gollarhatti, Bengaluru, the tempo traveller hit the iron wall as the vehicle was driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner which resulted in accident.
Due to accident, the vehicle toppled down and the inmates of vehicle, including the petitioner, sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to Prakriya Hospital, wherein she was treated conservatively and spent a sum of .2,00,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing Agriculture and earning a sum of .30,000/-.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of Tempo Traveller by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 did not appeared before the tribunal and hence he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through his counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of policy bearing No.MS338985 against tempo traveller which is valid from 22.12.2022 to 21.12.2023 and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the insured vehicle had been driven by person having no valid and effective driving license to drive the class of vehicle.
Further contended that the insured vehicle was plying without valid permit and FC at the place and time of alleged accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.
5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, she sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 04.01.2023 at about 04.45 a.m., nice road, near Kodigehalli Bridge,
Gollarahatti, Bengaluru, while she was travelling in a Tempo Traveller bearing Regn.No.KA- Sarswathamma vs Kumar Singh M.R on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127717423/
2 13-B-5706, due to the rash and negligent driving of above said vehicle and by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1,
MRD Technician of Prakriya Hospital, Nagasandra, Bengaluru, as PW.2 and Dr. Nagaraj.B.N working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19 and closed her side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce either oral or documentary evidence.

7. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

The petitioner contended that on 04.01.2023 at about 04.45 a.m., accident took place at nice road, near Kodigehalli Bridge, Gollarahatti, Bengaluru, while she was travelling in a Tempo Traveller bearing Regn.No.KA-13-B-5706, due to the rash and negligent driving of above said vehicle and by its driver in which she sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Tempo Traveller bearing Regn.No.KA-13-B- 5706 by its driver, the petitioner got examined as PW.1.
In the chief examination, she deposed that due to rash and negligent riding of Tempo Traveller by its driver, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited from PW.1 to disprove or disbelieve the case of petitioner.
Nothing to dispute or rebut the contention of petitioner related to the accident and cause of accident could be elicited during the cross examination.

11. Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the petitioner produced Ex.P.2 First Information statement lodged by one Gangappa, with the police on 04.01.2023.
On the basis of first information lodged by said Gangappa, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 of IPC.

In the first information statement as Sarswathamma vs Kumar Singh M.R on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127717423/
3 well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.

sentences.text: The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicle are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicle.
The said document clearly indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 338 of IPC as per Ex.P.7.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents placed no satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle has driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner that resulted in the accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.9, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Tempo Traveller bearing Regn.No.KA-13-B-5706 by its driver and same resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of holding issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.

Sarswathamma vs Kumar Singh M.R on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127717423/
4 i)
Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident, she sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.
In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by Prakriya Hospitals which is marked as Ex.P.5.
The said document discloses that the injuries sustained by petitioner are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner produced Ex.P.6 - discharge summary issued by Prakriya Hospitals, wherein she is stated to have taken treatment as an inpatient.
Petitioner examined Dr. Nagaraj B.N as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P18 & 19.

PW.3/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and the petitioner is stated to have disability to left arm to the extent of 30% and to the whole body to the extent of 10%.
PW.3 deposed that the petitioner is having wasting of left upper limb and restricted shoulder movements.
PW.3 stated that the whole body disability is 10%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .60,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that she took treatment at Hospital for the injuries.
The petitioner produced Medical bills for .1,04,532/- as per Ex.P.10 and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.11.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills produced by the petitioner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut the medical bills furnished by petitioner.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to controvert or rebut the bills furnished by petitioner.
So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .1,04,532/- appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 04.01.2023 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital due to the injuries sustained.
So, during the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.
The petitioner produced Ex.P.6 - Discharge Summary, wherein it discloses that the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 04.01.2023 to 07.01.2023 i.e., for a period of 4 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 4 days to a sum of .2,000/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:
The petitioner is a resident of Kaidala, Gulur, Tumkuru and she got admitted to hospital for treatment at Bangalore.
In order to prove this aspect the petitioner produced Discharge Summary.
Considering the injuries and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.

(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
Sarswathamma vs Kumar Singh M.R on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127717423/
5
The petitioner contended that she was working as an Agriculturist and earning a sum of .30,000/- per month.
In order to prove her income, the petitioner has not produced any document.
The petitioner not furnished any materials to show the nature of work done by her and to show that she was earning .30,000/- per month.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to substantiate the contention of petitioner related to her occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the notional income is to be taken into consideration.
On consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,000/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended her work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .30,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:
The petitioner contended that due to accident, she was admitted as an inpatient at hospital, and sustained permanent disablement.

The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N., working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center,
Bengaluru, as PW.3.

sentences.text: PW.3/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess the disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained D12 Wedge compression fracture, left clavicle fracture of the left 4th and 5th rib with lung contusion and was treated conservatively and later discharged.
The doctor has examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability to left arm to the extent of 30% and the whole body to the extent of 10%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.18 & 19 i.e., clinical report and X-ray film.

The petitioner also examined MRD Technician of Prakriya Hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.14 to 17 i.e., authorization letter, MLC Register Extract,
Police intimation and case sheet.
In the evidence, Pw-3 deposed that the fractures are united and the petitioner was stable at the time of discharge.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that there is loss in her earning capacity due to the injuries sustained by her.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that the petitioner suffered loss of income due to accidental injuries.
PW.3 stated that the petitioner is unable to lift weights and unable to do her routine work normally.
PW.3 also stated that the petitioner is having restricted left shoulder movements.

The counsel for respondent No.2 relied on decision rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.2973/2005 dated 19.07.2005 between North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation V/s Somappa Rudrappa Kuravinkoppa,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that in case of clavicle and mandible fractures, there would be no consequence loss of future earning capacity.

sentences.text: In the present case, the materials on record disclose that the petitioner sustained fracture to the left clavicle as well as left 4th and 5th rib with lung contusion.

As per the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, there will be no consequence of loss Sarswathamma vs Kumar Singh M.R on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127717423/
6 of earning capacity in case of fracture to the clavicle.

sentences.text: In the present case, the petitioner is having fracture to the left clavicle as well as ribs.

Though the petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards loss of future earning capacity related to the fracture of clavicle, she is considered to be entitled for compensation to the injuries sustained under the said head related to other injuries.
As per the materials on record, the petitioner appears to be a home maker.
The petitioner might require to do house hold work and the injuries sustained by her might affect in doing her house work to some extent though not completely.
The petitioner is stated to have sustained fracture to 4th and 5th rib.
It is stated by PW.3 that the petitioner is unable to lift weights and there is restricted shoulder movement which might affect the petitioner's day to day work.
As such, on considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do her work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 5%.

entities.text: Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove age of the petitioner, she has not produced any documents.
But in Ex.P.5 - Wound Certificate, the age of petitioner is mentioned as 50 years as on the date of accident.
The respondents not furnished any materials in order to disprove or rebut the age of petitioner appearing in the said document.

As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner appears to be 50 years as on the date of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier, in the absence of materials to the contrary.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case '13' multiplier is applicable.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble supreme court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of her gross income.

sentences.text:
Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,000/- x 12) = .1,92,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (5% of prior annual income) = .9,600/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 13 Loss of future earnings - (.9,600/- x 13) = .1,24,800/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .1,24,800/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and she is unable to do her day- today activities as earlier.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of Sarswathamma vs Kumar Singh M.R on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127717423/

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of .3,41,332/-.
15.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 & 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Tempo Traveller bearing Regn.No.KA-13-B- 5706 by its driver.
The issue of policy in favour of tempo traveller is being admitted by respondent No.2.
The materials on record disclose that the insurance policy is valid as on the date of accident.
As per the materials on record, the tempo traveller is duly insured with respondent No.2 and is valid as on the date of accident.

So, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending Sarswathamma vs Kumar Singh M.R on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127717423/
8 vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .3,41,332/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Forty One Thousand Three Hundred and Thirty Two only) with interest at 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.

Annual Income before accident : (.16,000/- x 12) = .1,92,000/-
Loss of future earning p.a. (5% of prior annual income) = .9,600/-.
Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 13 Loss of future earnings - (.9,600/- x 13) = .1,24,800/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .1,24,800/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and she is unable to do her day- today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of Sarswathamma vs Kumar Singh M.R on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127717423/
7 future amenities.
14.
The materials on record disclose that the insurance policy is valid as on the date of accident.
As per the materials on record, the tempo traveller is duly insured with respondent No.2 and is valid as on the date of accident.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the notional income is to be taken into consideration.
The counsel for respondent No.2 relied on decision rendered by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.2973/2005 dated 19.07.2005 between North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation V/s Somappa Rudrappa Kuravinkoppa,
wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that in case of clavicle and mandible fractures, there would be no consequence loss of future earning capacity.
In the present case, the petitioner is having fracture to the left clavicle as well as ribs.
Though the petitioner is not entitled for compensation towards loss of future earning capacity related to the fracture of clavicle, she is considered to be entitled for compensation to the injuries sustained under the said head related to other injuries.
